q: If instead the same P150,000,000 project were structured as Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost basis (10% RPF per Sec. 12.4.2), what would the fee be?
n: 10% x P150,000,000 = P15,000,000, per Sec. 12.4.2.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 12.4.2
scenario: Scenario: An Architect undertakes Design-Build Services by Administration (SPP Doc. 207) for a project with a Project Construction Cost of P150,000,000.

q: Which of the following is listed as a method of compensation for Pre-Design Services under Sec. 5.2?
n: Sec. 5.2.1-5.2.5 lists Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, Professional Fee Plus Expenses, Lump Sum/Fixed Fee, Per Diem/Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses, and Mixed Methods as compensation options for Pre-Design Services.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 5.2

q: Under Sec. 13.2.1, who nominates/appoints the Professional Advisor for an Architectural Design Competition (ADC), and who approves the appointment?
o: Nominated/appointed and paid by the Owner, approved by the IAPOA National Board of Directors (NBD)
Nominated by the Jury, approved by the Owner
Nominated by the Competition Secretariat, approved by the PRC
n: Sec. 13.2.1 states the Professional Advisor is an Architect nominated/appointed and paid by the Owner and approved by the IAPOA National Board of Directors through its ADC Committee.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 13.2.1

q: Under DAEDS or DADS, what happens to the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each State-regulated professional involved?
o: They remain separate; the Architect does not assume the responsibilities/liabilities of the other professionals (RLPs)
The Architect assumes all liabilities regardless of arrangement
They are pooled and shared equally among all professionals
Liability is transferred entirely to the Owner
n: Sec. 6.1 states that in both DAEDS and DADS, professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each State-regulated professional remain separate; the Architect does not assume the other RLPs' liabilities.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.1

q: Under Sec. 13.6.9, in a Project ADC, if no contract is signed within how many months of the Jury's award announcement, is the first prize winner entitled to an additional sum equal to the first prize?
n: Sec. 13.6.9 states the first prize winner receives a further sum equal to the first prize if no contract is signed within twelve (12) months of the announcement of the Jury's award.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 13.6.9

q: Which of the following building types is classified under Group 1 (simplest utilization/character) in Sec. 6.3.1?
n: Group 1 lists buildings of the simplest utilization and character requiring minimal architectural finishes, including armories, bakeries, hangars, parking structures, and warehouses.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.1

q: If the winning Competitor in a Project ADC is unable to satisfy the Jury of his/her ability to carry out the design, what happens under Sec. 13.6.6?
o: The competition is voided and re-run
The second-place entry automatically wins the commission
The Jury may require the winner to collaborate with another Architect of the winning Competitor's choice, duly approved by the Jury and Owner
n: Sec. 13.6.6 states the Jury may require the winner to collaborate with another Architect of the winning Competitor's own choice, approved by the Jury and Owner.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 13.6.6

q: A Group 1 warehouse project has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P80,000,000, contracted under DAEDS. Using the Group 1 fee schedule ('Over P50.0M to P100.0M: P2,500,000 plus 4% of excess of P50.0M'), what is the Recommended Professional Fee?
n: Excess over P50M = P80M - P50M = P30M; 4% x P30M = P1,200,000; RPF = P2,500,000 + P1,200,000 = P3,700,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.1 (Group 1 DAEDS Fee Table)
scenario: Scenario: A Group 1 warehouse (simplest utilization/character building) has a Project Construction Cost of P80,000,000, and is contracted under Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS).

q: Under Sec. 14.1.1.3, when a non-FPCA (a Foreign Architect or Foreign Consultant) is engaged because no qualified FPCA is available, how many Filipino RLAs in the same specialization must be employed as understudies?
n: Sec. 14.1.1.3 requires a minimum of two (2) Filipino RLAs in the same area/field of specialization to be employed as understudies when a non-FPCA is engaged.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 14.1.1.3

q: Which of the following buildings falls under Group 2 (moderate complexity of plan/design) per Sec. 6.3.2?
n: Group 2 lists moderately complex buildings including banks, schools, hospitals... actually Shopping Centers, Malls, Office Buildings, Schools, and similar structures, as opposed to Group 1's simplest utilization buildings.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.2

q: Which of the following is listed among the compensation methods for Professional Architectural Consulting Services under Sec. 14.2.2?
o: Only Lump Sum, with no other option allowed
n: Sec. 14.2.2.1-5 lists Per Diem/Hourly, Retainer, Salary cost times a multiplier plus direct/reimbursable cost, Fixed/Lump Sum payment, and Percentage of total project cost.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 14.2.2

q: For the same P150,000,000 Group 2 mall project, if contracted under DADS instead ('Over P100.0M to P200.0M: P3,300,000 plus 2.4% of excess of P100.0M'), what is the RPF?
n: Excess over P100M = P50M; 2.4% x P50M = P1,200,000; RPF = P3,300,000 + P1,200,000 = P4,500,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.2 (Group 2 DADS Fee Table)
scenario: Scenario: A Group 2 shopping mall has a Project Construction Cost of P150,000,000, contracted under Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS).

q: Under Sec. 16, the Architect is entitled to interest on unpaid fees, charges and reimbursements if payment is not made within how many days from receipt of billing?
n: Sec. 16 states the Architect is entitled to interest (at the prevailing BSP rate, mutually agreed with the Client) on amounts not paid within thirty (30) days from receipt of billing.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 16

q: A Group 3 hospital project has a PCC of P300,000,000 under DAEDS. Using the table ('Over P200.0M to P500.0M: P11,500,000 plus 4% of excess of P200.0M'), what is the RPF?
n: Excess over P200M = P100M; 4% x P100M = P4,000,000; RPF = P11,500,000 + P4,000,000 = P15,500,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.3 (Group 3 DAEDS Fee Table)
scenario: Scenario: A Group 3 hospital project (exceptional character/complexity building) has a Project Construction Cost of P300,000,000, contracted under DAEDS.

q: Under Sec. 19.2, if a dispute is not resolved within an initial 14-day negotiation period, the parties may engage in mediation/conciliatory discussions for how much additional time before seeking CIAC arbitration?
n: Sec. 19.2 provides for a further 14 calendar days of mediation/conciliatory discussions after the initial 14-day negotiation period fails, before parties may seek CIAC arbitration.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 19.2

q: For Group 4 residences, what is the Recommended Professional Fee for DAEDS, expressed as a percentage of PCC?
n: The Group 4 table states the RPF for DAEDS is 10% of PCC (and 6% of PCC for DADS).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.4 (Group 4)

q: Where is the exclusive venue for CIAC arbitration proceedings under Sec. 19.3?
o: CIAC Office at corners Sen. Gil Puyat Ave. and Makati Ave., Makati City
n: Sec. 19.3 fixes the exclusive venue as the CIAC Office at corners Sen. Gil Puyat Ave. and Makati Ave. in Makati City.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 19.3

q: For the same residence, if the Client instead contracts DADS (Architect handles architectural design only, engineers hired separately), what is the RPF at 6% of PCC?
n: Group 4 DADS RPF is 6% of PCC: 6% x P8,000,000 = P480,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.4 (Group 4)
scenario: Scenario: A Client commissions the design of a single-detached residence (Group 4 classification) with a Project Construction Cost of P8,000,000.

q: Under Sec. 21, any amendment to the Architect's Guidelines must be prepared by which body before submission to the UAP National Board for approval?
o: The Department of Trade and Industry
A Special Committee on the Standards of Professional Practice of the IAPOA, in consultation with the PRC-PRBoA
n: Sec. 21 states amendments shall be prepared by a Special Committee on the Standards of Professional Practice of the IAPOA, in consultation with the PRC-PRBoA and other architects' associations.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 21

q: A commemorative museum/monument (Group 5) has a PCC of P20,000,000 and is contracted under DADS. What is the Architect's RPF, at 7.5% of PCC?
n: Group 5 DADS RPF = 7.5% x P20,000,000 = P1,500,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.5 (Group 5)
scenario: Scenario: A commemorative museum/monument project (Group 5 classification) has a Project Construction Cost of P20,000,000, contracted under Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS).

q: Per Annex A, 'Cost of Work (CoW)' is used specifically for which category of projects?
o: Architectural interiors, acoustics, lighting works, site development, and landscaping under Specialized Architectural Services
n: Annex A defines Cost of Work as the total cost of fixtures/accessories for architectural interiors, acoustics, lighting, site development/landscaping designed by the Specialist Architect/SCs — used for Specialized Architectural Services projects.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Cost of Work)

q: A developer builds 4 identical warehouse buildings from one set of plans (Group 6, repetitive design), where the RPF for one building's full design (as computed under Group 1) is P2,000,000. What is the TOTAL Architect's fee for all 4 buildings, applying the Group 6 repetitive-use schedule (100%/50%/40%/30%)?
scenario: Scenario: A developer builds 4 identical warehouse buildings using one set of plans/design (Group 6, repetitive construction). The RPF for the full design of one such building, as computed under its building group, is P2,000,000.

q: Per Annex A, the value of the 'multiplier' may range from what to what, depending on office set-up, project complexity, experience, and geographic area?
n: Annex A states the multiplier value may range from 1.5 to 2.5, consistent with Sec. 4.3.8.2's Multiple of DPE range.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Multiplier)

q: Continuing Group 7, for units 11 to 30 in a Housing Project (DAEDS), the fee is computed as the fee for 10 units plus what percentage of RPF for each additional unit?
n: The Group 7 table states: 'Eleven to thirty units (11-30): Fee for 10 units plus 40% of RPF for each additional unit' under DAEDS.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.7 (Group 7)

q: Per Annex A, 'Project Development Cost' includes construction cost, professional fees, permits, clearances/utilities, and additionally which of the following?
o: The BSP prevailing interest rate on late payments
Cost of acquiring the project site/lot and cost of money
n: Annex A defines Project Development Cost as including construction cost, all professional fees, permits, clearances and utilities, cost of acquiring the project site/lot, and cost of money.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Project Development Cost)

q: Continuing that scenario, what is the TOTAL fee for all 15 units (the 10-unit fee of P2,750,000 plus the remaining 5 units at 40% of RPF each, per the 11-30 unit bracket)?
n: Additional fee for units 11-15 (5 units) = 5 x 40% x P500,000 = 5 x P200,000 = P1,000,000. Total = P2,750,000 + P1,000,000 = P3,750,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.7 (Group 7 Housing Project schedule)
scenario: Scenario: A Client commissions a Housing Project of 15 identical single-detached units built from one set of plans/design (Group 7 classification), contracted under DAEDS. The Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for one unit alone is P500,000.

q: Per Annex A, the 'Prime Professional' is defined as the Architect who is commissioned to plan/design the building and to do what regarding other design professionals?
o: Supervise only the structural engineer's work
Coordinate the works of all allied design professionals involved, ensuring compatibility with the architectural design concept
Pay their fees directly out of his own compensation
Assume full civil liability for their work
n: Annex A defines Prime Professional as the Architect who plans/designs the building and coordinates the works of all allied design professionals, ensuring compliance with project requirements and compatibility with the design concept.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Prime Professional)

q: A built-in cabinetry and architectural interiors project (Group 8) has a PCC of P5,000,000. What is the Architect's RPF?
n: Group 8 RPF = 15% x P5,000,000 = P750,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.8 (Group 8)
scenario: Scenario: A project involving extensive detail (built-in components, special fittings, and architectural interiors, Group 8 classification) has a Project Construction Cost of P5,000,000.

q: Per Annex B, what does 'SPPCC' stand for?
o: Special Provision for Project Construction Cost
Standard Professional Percentage of Construction Cost
Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost
Schedule of Professional Payments for Construction Contracts
n: Annex B lists SPPCC as 'Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex B (Acronyms)

q: An office building (Group 2) is being renovated; its PCC is P60,000,000 and a new-construction DAEDS RPF, computed under the Group 2 table ('Over P50.0M to P100.0M: P3,000,000 plus 5% of excess of P50.0M'), would be P3,500,000. Applying the Group 9 renovation surcharge of 150% of RPF, what is the actual chargeable fee?
n: 150% x P3,500,000 = P5,250,000, applying the Group 9 alteration/renovation surcharge.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.2 and Sec. 6.3.9 (Group 9 renovation surcharge)
scenario: Scenario: An existing office building (Group 2 classification) undergoing renovation has a PCC of P60,000,000. Its equivalent new-construction DAEDS RPF, computed under the Group 2 table, is P3,500,000.

q: Per the Sample Fee Calculation Worksheets (Annexes D and E), what percentage of the Base Fee is allocated to the Schematic Design Phase?
n: Both the DAEDS (Annex D) and DADS (Annex E) sample worksheets allocate 15% of the Base Fee to the Schematic Design Phase (5% Project Definition, 15% Schematic Design, 20% Design Development, 50% Contract Documents, 10% Construction), matching the Sec. 6.4 payment-phase percentages.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex D/E (Sample Fee Calculation Worksheets)

q: Still under Group 10, when the Architect renders services as an EXPERT WITNESS, the fee shall not be less than how much per appearance, regardless of whether the hearing took place?
n: Sec. 6.3.10 states the Architect's fee for expert-witness appearances shall not be less than Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) per appearance, regardless of whether the scheduled hearing took place.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.10 (Group 10)

q: An Architect is engaged for a project where the scope keeps evolving and costs are hard to predetermine in advance, such as experimental/investigative work. Which method of compensation, per Sec. 4.3.11.2, is 'best suited' for such projects?
o: Salary Cost times a Multiplier plus Reimbursable Expenses
n: Sec. 4.3.11.2 states the Salary method 'is best suited for Projects for which the costs are difficult to predetermine, or in cases where it may become necessary to undertake additional experimental or investigative work.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.11.2

q: An Architect renders a Group 10 technical opinion service requiring 3 hours of consultation at the minimum rate of P1,000.00/hour, at a project site 250 km from her office (thus subject to the 60% travel surcharge). What is her TOTAL fee?
n: Base fee = 3 hours x P1,000 = P3,000.00; travel surcharge = 60% x P3,000 = P1,800.00; total = P3,000 + P1,800 = P4,800.00.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.10 (Group 10)
scenario: Scenario: An Architect renders a Group 10 technical opinion/advisory service requiring 3 hours of work, billed at the minimum RPF of P1,000.00 per hour, at a site located 250 km (straight-line) from her office.

q: An Architect is asked to appear before the CIAC as an expert witness in a fee dispute, and the hearing is later postponed. Per Sec. 6.3.10, is she still entitled to her minimum fee?
o: Yes, the minimum P5,000.00 fee is due per appearance regardless of whether the scheduled hearing took place
Only 50% of the fee is due
No, since the hearing did not push through, no fee is due
She may only claim reimbursement of travel costs, not the appearance fee
n: Sec. 6.3.10 explicitly states the expert-witness fee (not less than P5,000.00 per appearance) is due 'regardless as to whether the scheduled hearing took place or not.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.10 (Group 10)

q: Upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase, the Owner pays a sum sufficient to bring the TOTAL cumulative payments to what percentage of the Professional Fee?
n: Sec. 6.4.2 states the payment brings the cumulative total to twenty (20.0%) percent of the Professional Fee.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.2

q: What document number is assigned to the Architect's Guidelines for SPP Compliances on the Methods of Compensation and Schedule of Fees?
n: Section 1 (Title) names the document 'UAP-IAPOA DOC. 210: ARCHITECT'S GUIDELINES FOR STANDARDS OF PROFESSIONAL PRACTICE (SPP) COMPLIANCES - METHODS OF COMPENSATION AND SCHEDULE OF FEES.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 1 (UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210)

q: A Client and Architect agree on a Professional Fee (PF) of P5,000,000 for Regular Design Services. Following Sec. 6.4's cumulative payment schedule, how much is due upon signing of the Service Agreement (5% of PF)?
n: 5% x P5,000,000 = P250,000, per Sec. 6.4.1.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.1
scenario: Scenario: A Client and Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of P5,000,000 for Regular Design Services, to be paid per the Sec. 6.4 cumulative payment schedule (5% / 20% / 40% / 90% / 90% / 100% cumulative).

q: Under which PRBoA issuance was this Architect's Guidelines document (Annex A) approved, adopted and promulgated in 2016?
n: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture approved, adopted and promulgated the Architect's Guidelines through PRBoA Resolution No. 06, Series of 2016, published in the Official Gazette (Vol. 112, No. 38, Sept. 19, 2016).  Source: PRBoA Resolution No. 06, s. 2016

q: Continuing that scenario, upon completion of the Contract Document Phase, cumulative payments should reach 90% of the PF. How much ADDITIONAL payment is due at that stage (from the prior 40% cumulative)?
n: Cumulative target = 90% x P5,000,000 = P4,500,000; already paid (40%) = P2,000,000; additional due = P4,500,000 - P2,000,000 = P2,500,000, matching the 50% increment in Sec. 6.4.4.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.4
scenario: Scenario: A Client and Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of P5,000,000 for Regular Design Services, to be paid per the Sec. 6.4 cumulative payment schedule (5% / 20% / 40% / 90% / 90% / 100% cumulative).

q: Which body was tasked, under PRBoA Resolution No. 3, s. 2010, with developing the Architect's Guidelines on Methods of Compensation and Schedule of Fees?
o: The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA/UAP)
n: PRBoA Resolution No. 3, s. 2010 directed the IAPOA (United Architects of the Philippines) to develop the Architect's Guidelines on the Methods of Compensation and Schedule of Fees.  Source: Foreword / PRBoA Resolution No. 03, s. 2010

q: Per Sec. 6.4.9, if the Owner fails to implement the plans/documents prepared by the Architect after the Detailed Design and Contract Documents Phase is complete, what percentage of the Architect's fee is he entitled to receive?
n: Sec. 6.4.9 states that once the Architect has completed the Detailed Design and Contract Documents Phase (equivalent to 90% of his work), he is entitled to ninety percent (90%) of the Architect's fee if the Owner fails to implement the plans.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.9

q: Which historical association first laid the groundwork for standards of architectural practice fees in the Philippines, in 1933?
n: The Postscript states the groundwork was laid on January 21, 1933 by the Philippine Architects Society (PAS), entitled 'Relation of Charges and Rules Relative to Professional Fees.'  Source: Postscript

q: Which of the following is NOT among the Fee Adjustment Factors listed in Sec. 6.5?
o: Project Delivery Method and Construction Procurement
Renovation to Existing Buildings (versus New Construction)
n: Sec. 6.5 lists factors (a) through (o) including scope of services, delivery method, schedules, documentation/BIM, specialist consultants, approvals, submittals, new technologies, construction administration, site conditions, renovation vs. new construction, repeat work, personnel, demobilization/remobilization, and phased occupancies — none relate to astrology.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.5

q: The purpose of the Architect's Guidelines, as stated in the Rationale (Sec. 2), is best described as which of the following?
o: A purely internal UAP membership directory
A replacement for RA 9266 that supersedes the Architecture Act
A criminal statute penalizing unlicensed architectural practice
A complement to existing regulatory law that standardizes the ranges for Client compensation of Architects
n: Sec. 2.1 states the Guidelines standardize the ranges by which a Client compensates an Architect and complement the existing regulatory law without unduly affecting it.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 2 (Rationale)

q: Under Sec. 7 (Specialized Architectural Services, SPP Doc. 203), the term 'Architect' refers to the Consulting Architect (CA) who may hold what kind of certificate?
o: A valid Specialist Certificate issued by the Board/Commission upon due qualification/accreditation by the IAPOA
n: Sec. 7 states that for Specialized Architectural Services, 'Architect' refers to the Consulting Architect (CA) who may hold a valid Specialist Certificate issued by the Board and/or Commission upon due qualification or accreditation by the IAPOA.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7

q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the criteria to be considered in Sec. 3.2 when computing professional fees?
o: Studies, programs and other professional input furnished by the Owner
Probability of contingencies not included in cost estimates
n: Sec. 3.2.1-3.2.6 lists time schedules, owner-furnished studies, client's review/approval procedure, costs of administration, probability of contingencies, and number of third parties to be consulted — marital status is not a criterion.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 3.2

q: If the Owner/Client separately hires other Specialist Consultants (SCs) for a specialized architectural project, what fee does the Architect earn for coordinating their work with the design concept?
o: A flat P50,000 regardless of project size
n: Sec. 7.2.3 states the Architect's fee for coordinating and relating the work of the Specialist Consultant to the design concept will be 5% of the SC's fee.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.2.3

q: Under the Percentage-based Fee method, the Professional Fee (PF) of the Architect is determined by:
o: Multiplying floor area by the Architect's hourly rate
Dividing the PCC by the number of design phases
Multiplying the specified percentage times the Project Construction Cost (PCC)
Adding a fixed multiplier of 2.5 to the PCC
n: Sec. 4.1.1.2 states the PF is determined by multiplying the specified percentage times the estimated, awarded, or final Project Construction Cost (PCC).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.2

q: Per Sec. 7.3.1.1, the Recommended Professional Fee for Architectural Interior, Acoustic Design, Architectural Lighting Layout and Design, and Site Development Planning ranges from:
o: 10% to 15% of the cost of work
5% to 8% of the cost of work
15% to 20% of the cost of work
12% to 18% of the cost of work
n: Sec. 7.3.1.1 states the RPF for these Specialized Architectural Services is 10% to 15% of the cost of work, depending on complexity.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.1.1

q: An architect quotes her fee using the winning contractor's bid amount as the basis for the Project Construction Cost. Which specific cost basis is she using?
o: Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost (SPPCC)
n: Sec. 4.1.1.3.2 defines the Awarded Project Construction Cost (APCC) as that using the bid of the winning contractor.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.3.2

q: Per the physical planning fee table (Sec. 7.3.2), what is the basic rate per square meter for the first 5 hectares or less?
n: The table states the basic rate for the first 5 hectares or less is P5.00 per sq. meter (1 hectare = 10,000 sq. meters, consistent with P50,000/hectare).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.2 (Physical Planning fee table)

q: For a project handled under DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services), what percentage of the corresponding DAEDS professional fee does the architectural design services portion constitute?
n: Sec. 4.1.1.5 states the architectural design services shall constitute sixty percent (60%) of the corresponding stated professional fee (PF) for DAEDS for the project.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.5

q: If, instead, that same 8-hectare site is rugged with steep terrain (a 20% fee increase applies per Sec. 7.3.2.2), what would the adjusted RPF be, based on the flat-terrain RPF of P370,000.00?
n: Adjusted RPF = P370,000 x 1.20 = P444,000.00, applying the minimum 20% increase for rugged/steep terrain under Sec. 7.3.2.2.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.2.2
scenario: Scenario: A physical planning engagement (Site Development Planning, Sec. 7.3.2) covers a total land area of 8 hectares. Assume this particular site is rugged with steep terrain rather than moderately flat.

q: A high-rise office building project has 10,000 sqm gross floor area (GFA) and 2,000 sqm non-GFA. The average Project Construction Cost is P30,000.00/sqm, and the applicable percentage for professional fee based on PCC is 6%. What is the professional fee PER SQUARE METER of GFA under the Unit Cost Method?
n: PF per sqm = P30,000.00 x 0.06 = P1,800.00/sqm, exactly as worked in the Sec. 4.1.2 Unit Cost Method example.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.2 (Unit Cost Method example)
scenario: Scenario (Unit Cost Method worked example): A high-rise office building project has 10,000 sqm gross floor area (GFA) and 2,000 sqm non-GFA. Average Project Construction Cost (based on historical data) is P30,000.00/sqm, and the Professional Fee based on Percentage of PCC is 6%.

q: Under Sec. 7.3.3, basic compensation for 'Other Specialized Architectural Services' (extra/additional services) is computed through man-months based on how many man-hours per man-day?
n: Sec. 7.3.3 states compensation is computed through man-months, i.e., 22 man-days multiplied by 8 man-hours, multiplied by a factor to cover overhead.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.3

q: An architect is asked to design a similar high-rise office building with 8,000 sqm GFA and 1,500 sqm non-GFA. Using an average construction cost of P25,000/sqm and the same 5% Unit Cost Method percentage, what is the Professional Fee for the GFA portion alone?
n: PF/sqm = P25,000 x 0.05 = P1,250/sqm; PF for GFA = P1,250/sqm x 8,000 sqm = P10,000,000.00, applying the same Unit Cost Method as Sec. 4.1.2.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.2 (Unit Cost Method)
scenario: Scenario: An office building project has 8,000 sqm gross floor area (GFA) and 1,500 sqm non-GFA. Average Project Construction Cost is P25,000.00/sqm, and the applicable percentage for professional fee based on PCC is 5%.

q: A project with a PCC of P40,000,000 engages an Architect for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services. Using the 1% to 1.5% RPF range, what is the LOWEST reasonable fee?
n: Lowest RPF = 1% x P40,000,000 = P400,000, per Sec. 8.3.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 8.3
scenario: Scenario: A project with a Project Construction Cost of P40,000,000 engages a Consulting Architect for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A).

q: Value-based Pricing/Percentage of Gross Rentals, as a method of compensation, is most appropriate for which type of engagement?
o: Building Administration and Management Services where the Architect innovates schemes for maximum occupancy and efficient building operation
n: Sec. 4.1 explains that for Building Administration and Management Services, where the Architect goes beyond maintenance to maximize occupancy and performance, remuneration may be based on a percentage of gross rentals.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1 (Value-based Pricing)

q: Under Sec. 8.5, if the Client separately hires a Consultant for full-time supervision-related work, what coordination fee does the Architect-of-Record (AoR) earn?
o: No coordination fee is provided for
n: Sec. 8.5 states the AoR's coordination fee for relating the Consultant's work to the Architect's work is 5% of the Consultant's fee, mirroring Sec. 7.2.3.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 8.5

q: Under Time-based fees (Sec. 4.3), which of the following is NOT listed as a typical use case?
o: Full-blown DAEDS services for a P1 billion mixed-use tower
Services which are not well defined
n: Sec. 4.3.2 lists undefined/partial/additional services, pre-design services, and expert-witness/specialist consultancy work as typical time-based engagements — not large, fully defined DAEDS contracts, which are typically percentage-based.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.2

q: A P100,000,000 project engages a Construction Manager under Sec. 9.3's 1.5%-3% range. What is the fee range in pesos?
scenario: Scenario: A project with a Project Construction Cost of P100,000,000 engages the Architect as Construction Manager (SPP Doc. 204-B).

q: Under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method (Sec. 4.3.8), the multiplier used to cover overhead and profit typically ranges from:
n: Sec. 4.3.8.2 states the multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5 depending on office set-up, overhead, experience, and project complexity.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.8.2

q: Which construction management contracting concept adjusts the fee via 'sharing formulas' applied to the difference between final allowable costs and target costs?
o: Cost Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF) or Cost Plus Adjusted Fee (CPAF)
n: Sec. 9.2.2.5 describes CPIF/CPAF as cost-reimbursement contracts with provisions for a fee adjusted by 'sharing' formulas applied to the difference between final allowable costs and target costs.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 9.2.2.5

q: Continuing that scenario, if Reimbursable Expenses (R) of P50,000 are also billed, what is the Total Cost of Service charged to the Client?
n: Total Cost of Service = Fee + R = P800,000 + P50,000 = P850,000, per the formula in Sec. 4.3.8.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.8 (Formula)
scenario: Scenario: An architectural office computes a Direct Cost (Architect + Consultant + Technical staff hourly charges, i.e. An + Cn + Tn) of P400,000 for a project, using a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit.

q: A commercial building generates gross monthly rental income of P2,000,000. Using the Sec. 10.3 value-pricing method (4%-6% of gross rental), what is the LOWEST monthly management fee?
n: Lowest fee = 4% x P2,000,000 = P80,000/month, per Sec. 10.3.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 10.3
scenario: Scenario: A commercial building under Post-Construction/Building Administration Services generates gross monthly rental income of P2,000,000.

q: A firm's total basic salaries (Direct Salary Expenses) for Professional Consulting Architects and staff assigned to a project amount to P300,000. Applying the Sec. 4.3.11 multiplier of 3.0 and adding P50,000 in reimbursable expenses, what is the total Fee?
n: Fee = Salary Cost x Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses = (P300,000 x 3.0) + P50,000 = P900,000 + P50,000 = P950,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.11 (Formula)
scenario: Scenario: A firm's Direct Salary Expenses (total basic salaries) of the PCAs and staff assigned to a project total P300,000, and the firm bills Reimbursable Expenses of P50,000 for the same engagement.

q: A P200,000,000 project engages the Architect as Project Manager under Comprehensive Architectural Services. Using the 2%-5% RPF range, what is the fee range?
scenario: Scenario: A P200,000,000 project engages the Architect as Project Manager under Comprehensive Architectural Services (SPP Doc. 206).

q: Under Sec. 4.4 (Mixed Methods of Compensation), which statement is correct?
o: Mixed methods can only be used for government projects
An assortment of compensation methods may be used within a single project, applying different methods to different phases or services
Mixed methods are prohibited under the Architect's Guidelines
Only a single method of compensation may be used per project, without exception
n: Sec. 4.4.1-4.4.4 states there is no reason an assortment of compensation methods should not be used if appropriate in a single project, citing examples like Pre-Design/Construction on DPE while Regular Design is on percentage of PCC.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.4 (Mixed Methods)

q: Under Sec. 12.4.1, the Recommended Professional Fee for Design-Build Services BY ADMINISTRATION is what percentage of PCC (exclusive of the Regular Design Services fee)?
n: Sec. 12.4.1 states the RPF for Design-Build Services by Administration is 7% of the PCC, exclusive of the Architect's Fee for Regular Design Services.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 12.4.1

q: Which SPP Document number corresponds to Construction Management Services?
n: Construction Management Services corresponds to SPP Doc. 204-B, distinct from Full-Time Construction Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Rule III / Sec. 9

q: An Architect undertakes Design-Build Services by Administration for a project with a PCC of P150,000,000. Applying the 7% RPF under Sec. 12.4.1, what is the Design-Build fee (exclusive of Regular Design Services)?
n: 7% x P150,000,000 = P10,500,000, per Sec. 12.4.1.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 12.4.1
scenario: Scenario: An Architect undertakes Design-Build Services by Administration (SPP Doc. 207) for a project with a Project Construction Cost of P150,000,000.

q: Within how many calendar days from submission of the statement of account must the Client make progress payments for Pre-Design Services, upon the Architect's request?
n: Sec. 5.3 states the Client shall make progress payments upon request of the Architect within seven (7) calendar days from submission of the statement of account.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 5.3

q: Under Sec. 12.2.2.2, whatever mode of construction involvement the Architect adopts under Design-Build Services, he/she must strictly adhere to the tenets of which document?
n: Sec. 12.2.2.2 requires strict adherence to the tenets of the Architects Credo, including disclosure of any conflict-of-interest business investment or venture.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 12.2.2.2

q: Under Sec. 6.1, what is the key structural difference between DAEDS and DADS contracting arrangements for Regular Design Services?
o: DADS assigns the Architect's civil liability to the engineers
DAEDS is only for government projects
There is no structural difference, only a difference in fee percentage
DAEDS uses a single contract between Architect and Owner with sub-consultancy agreements; DADS has the Architect and engineering/allied professionals execute separate contracts with the Owner
n: Sec. 6.1.1-6.1.2 describes DAEDS as a single Architect-Owner contract with sub-consultancy contracts, while DADS has the Architect and other professionals executing separate contracts directly with the Owner.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.1

q: Per Sec. 13.4.2, the Jury for an ADC consists of a majority of which group, assisted by a lay Juror representing the Owner?
n: Sec. 13.4.2 states the Jury consists of a majority of registered and licensed architects (RLAs), assisted by a lay Juror to represent the Owner's intention.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 13.4.2

q: Under Sec. 6.3, professional architectural work is classified into groups mainly to determine what?
o: The fair remuneration (RPF) for the Architect based on complexity/creative skill required
The Architect's required years of experience
The applicable BSP interest rate on late payments
n: Sec. 6.3 states a grouping of buildings is provided 'to determine the fair remuneration for the Architect,' based on the degree of complexity and creative skill required.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3

q: Per Sec. 13.6.4, within what period must the Owner pay the prizes allotted after the official announcement of ADC results?
n: Sec. 13.6.4 states the Owner undertakes to pay the prizes allotted within one (1) month of the official announcement of the ADC results.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 13.6.4

q: For a Group 1 building with a Project Construction Cost of P50.0 million or less, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS)?
n: The Group 1 fee schedule states 'P50.0 million and less: 5%' for DAEDS.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.1 (Group 1 Fee Table)

q: Under Sec. 14.1.1.1, a Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA) must be which of the following?
o: A Philippine-registered and licensed architect (RLA) who is a member in good standing of the IAPOA
A foreign national with a temporary special permit
A person holding only a DTI business registration
Any UAP member regardless of license status
n: Sec. 14.1.1.1 defines the FPCA as a Filipino citizen who is a Philippine-registered and licensed architect (RLA) and a member in good standing of the IAPOA.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 14.1.1.1

q: Using the same Group 1 warehouse project, if instead contracted under DADS ('Over P50.0M to P100.0M: P1,500,000 plus 2.4% of excess of P50.0M'), what is the Recommended Professional Fee?
n: Excess over P50M = P30M; 2.4% x P30M = P720,000; RPF = P1,500,000 + P720,000 = P2,220,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.1 (Group 1 DADS Fee Table)
scenario: Scenario: A Group 1 warehouse (simplest utilization/character building) has a Project Construction Cost of P80,000,000, and is contracted under Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS).

q: For Government projects, the selection of Professional Consulting Architects (PCAs) shall be in accordance with which law, per Sec. 14.1.1.4?
n: Sec. 14.1.1.4 states the selection of PCAs for Government projects shall follow RA 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act (GPRA) of 2003.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 14.1.1.4

q: A Group 2 shopping mall has a Project Construction Cost of P150,000,000, contracted under DAEDS. Using the Group 2 table ('Over P100.0M to P200.0M: P5,500,000 plus 4% of excess of P100.0M'), what is the RPF?
n: Excess over P100M = P50M; 4% x P50M = P2,000,000; RPF = P5,500,000 + P2,000,000 = P7,500,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.2 (Group 2 DAEDS Fee Table)
scenario: Scenario: A Group 2 shopping mall has a Project Construction Cost of P150,000,000, contracted under Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS).

q: Per Sec. 15, it is unlawful for whom to collect a fee for architectural services?
o: Any foreign consultant with a TSP
Any IAPOA member in good standing
n: Sec. 15 states it shall be unlawful for any unlicensed and unregistered person to collect a fee for architectural services, per RA 9266.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 15

q: Which of the following belongs to Group 3 (exceptional character and complexity) per Sec. 6.3.3?
n: Group 3 covers buildings of exceptional character/complexity requiring comparatively large amounts of research, such as airports, hospitals, hotels, laboratories, and stadia.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.3

q: Under Sec. 17, who bears the burden of Value-Added Tax (VAT) that government imposes as a consequence of the Architect's services?
o: The Owner/Client, since the Architect's fee is stated net to the Architect
The Architect, deducted from his net fee
It is split 50/50 between Architect and Owner
Neither party; VAT is waived for architectural services
n: Sec. 17 states the Architect's fee is net to the Architect, and any tax (exclusive of income tax), i.e., VAT, imposed as a consequence of services shall be paid by the Owner.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 17

q: Group 4 of the fee schedule (Sec. 6.3.4) covers which building type?
o: Residences (single-detached, single-attached or duplex; row-houses; small apartments; townhouses)
n: Group 4 covers residences (single-detached, single-attached or duplex; row-houses or shop-houses), small apartment houses and townhouses.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.4 (Group 4)

q: Under Sec. 19.2, the Construction Industry Arbitration Commission (CIAC) guarantees resolution of a dispute within what period?
n: Sec. 19.2 states the CIAC guarantees a resolution within a six (6) month period, after which the losing party may file a Petition for Review before the Court of Appeals.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 19.2

q: A Client commissions a single-detached residence (Group 4) with a PCC of P8,000,000 under DAEDS. What is the Architect's Recommended Professional Fee?
n: Group 4 DAEDS RPF is 10% of PCC: 10% x P8,000,000 = P800,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.4 (Group 4)
scenario: Scenario: A Client commissions the design of a single-detached residence (Group 4 classification) with a Project Construction Cost of P8,000,000.

q: Under Sec. 20 (Penalty Clause and Sanction), an unqualified individual/firm engaging in architectural services in violation of RA 9266 is subject to sanction 'without prejudice to' what?
o: The filing of appropriate criminal, civil, or other administrative cases
A one-time warning only, with no further action
n: Sec. 20 states such violators are subject to sanctions 'without prejudice to the filing of appropriate criminal, civil or other administrative or cases pursuant to existing laws.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 20

q: Group 5 of the fee schedule (Sec. 6.3.5) covers 'monumental buildings requiring consummate design skill and much precise detailing,' such as museums, memorials and mausoleums. What is the DAEDS RPF for Group 5?
n: The Group 5 table states the RPF for DAEDS is 12% of PCC (7.5% of PCC for DADS).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.5 (Group 5)

q: Per Annex A, the term 'Architect' as used in this Guideline refers only to a person holding what?
o: A UAP membership card only, regardless of PRC registration
An academic degree in architecture, regardless of licensure
A DTI business permit for architectural consulting
A valid certificate of registration and valid professional identification card as a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA)
n: Annex A (i) defines 'Architect' as a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA), a natural person with a valid certificate of registration and valid professional ID card (renewable 3-year license).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Definition of Terms)

q: Under Group 6 (Sec. 6.3.6), when a plan/design is re-used for repetitive construction of similar buildings without amending the drawings, what percentage of the RPF is charged for the SECOND building?
n: The Group 6 schedule states: 1st Building = 100% of RPF, 2nd Building = 50% of RPF, 3rd Building = 40% of RPF, 4th and succeeding = 30% of RPF.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.6 (Group 6)

q: Per Annex A, the 'Multiplier' compensates the Architect for which of the following? (Select the option that best matches the listed items.)
o: Only the Architect's personal income tax
Overhead costs, fringe benefits/social charges, contingency fees, interest on capital reserves, and reasonable profit
n: Annex A lists the Multiplier as compensating for: (a) overhead costs, (b) fringe benefits and social charges, (c) fee for contingencies, (d) interest on capital reserves, and (e) reasonable profit.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Multiplier)

q: Under Group 7 (Sec. 6.3.7), for a Housing Project of 2 to 10 units using one set of plans, the DAEDS fee is computed as the fee for one unit plus what percentage of the RPF for each additional unit?
n: The Group 7 table states: 'From two to ten units (2-10): Fee for one unit plus 50% of RPF for each additional unit' under DAEDS.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.7 (Group 7)

q: Per Annex A, 'Project Construction Cost (PCC)' EXCLUDES which of the following?
o: Materials and labor cost for installation
The fees for the Architect, Engineer, Specialist Consultants, or salaries of construction inspectors
n: Annex A explicitly states the PCC does not include any of the fees for the Architect, the Engineer, the Specialist Consultants, or the salaries of the construction inspectors.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Project Construction Cost)

q: A Client commissions a Housing Project of 15 identical single-detached units (Group 4 residence design, one set of plans) using DAEDS. The RPF for one unit (10% of its unit PCC) is P500,000. Using the Group 7 schedule, what is the fee for the FIRST TEN units combined (1st unit at full RPF, plus units 2-10 at 50% of RPF each)?
n: Fee for 10 units = RPF for unit 1 (P500,000) + [9 additional units x 50% x P500,000] = P500,000 + (9 x P250,000) = P500,000 + P2,250,000 = P2,750,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.7 (Group 7 Housing Project schedule)
scenario: Scenario: A Client commissions a Housing Project of 15 identical single-detached units built from one set of plans/design (Group 7 classification), contracted under DAEDS. The Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for one unit alone is P500,000.

q: Per Annex A, which of the following is explicitly listed as an example of a Reimbursable Expense?
o: The Architect's professional liability insurance premium
Cost of printing extra sets of drawings/reports over the required number of copies submitted to the Client
n: Annex A lists reimbursable expenses including cost of printing extra sets of drawings/reports/documents beyond the required copies, communication expenses, technical/laboratory tests, licenses/fees/taxes, and similar project-specific costs.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Reimbursable Expenses)

q: Under Group 8 (Sec. 6.3.8), which covers projects with extensive detail such as built-in components, special fittings, and architectural interiors, what is the Recommended Professional Fee?
n: Sec. 6.3.8 states the RPF for Group 8 (extensive detail projects) is 15% of the PCC.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.8 (Group 8)

q: Per Annex B (Acronyms), what does 'RPF' stand for?
n: Annex B lists RPF as 'Recommended Professional Fee.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex B (Acronyms)

q: Under Group 9 (Sec. 6.3.9), for alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit and expansion/additions to existing Group 1-5 buildings, the compensation is increased to what total percentage of the RPF?
n: Sec. 6.3.9 states compensation for such alteration/renovation/retrofit services should be increased by fifty percent (50%), for a total of one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the RPF.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.9 (Group 9)

q: Per Annex C (Related Laws), which Republic Act is the Government Procurement Reform Act of 2003?
n: Annex C lists R.A. No. 9184 as the Government Procurement Reform Act of 2003.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex C (Related Laws)

q: Under Group 10 (Sec. 6.3.10), where the Architect renders opinion, advice, or clarification on technical matters, the chargeable RPF shall NOT be less than how much per hour?
n: Sec. 6.3.10 states the chargeable RPF for rendering opinion/advice shall not be less than One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00) per hour.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.10 (Group 10)

q: Per the Sample Fee Calculation Worksheets, what percentage of the Base Fee is allocated to the Contract Document Phase?
n: Both sample worksheets (Annex D for DAEDS, Annex E for DADS) allocate 50% of the Base Fee to the Contract Document Phase.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex D/E (Sample Fee Calculation Worksheets)

q: For Group 10 services rendered at a location beyond 100 kilometers (air/straight-line/radial distance) from the Architect's office, what additional percentage is charged for the travel period?
n: Sec. 6.3.10 states another sixty percent (60%) of the amount shall be charged for the travel period for locations in excess of 100 km from the Architect's office.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.10 (Group 10)

q: A Client wants cost certainty from the outset and both parties can clearly and fully define the scope of services at the start of the project. Which method of compensation, per Sec. 4.2.1, is most appropriate?
n: Sec. 4.2.1 states Lump Sum/Fixed Fee 'may be used when the scope of services required can be clearly and fully defined at the outset of the project.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.2.1

q: Under Sec. 6.4.1, upon signing of the Service Agreement, what percentage of the agreed Professional Fee is paid to the Architect as engagement/acceptance fee?
n: Sec. 6.4.1 states an amount equivalent to 5% of the agreed Professional Fee shall be paid upon signing as the engagement/acceptance fee covering the mobilization component.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.1

q: A Client wants the Architect to also serve as Construction Manager on a project. Per Sec. 9.2, how should this additional role be compensated relative to the Architect's regular design services?
o: Since construction management is not part of the Architect's regular services, it shall be separately compensated
It may only be compensated via a retainer, no other method is allowed
It is a role reserved exclusively for licensed engineers, never architects
It is absorbed into the regular design fee at no extra cost, since it is part of the Architect's normal duties
n: Sec. 9.2 states that since construction management is not part of the regular services of the Architect, services rendered as Construction Manager shall be separately compensated.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 9.2

q: Upon completion of the Design Development Phase, cumulative payments to the Architect should total what percentage of the Professional Fee?
n: Sec. 6.4.3 states the payment increases the total cumulative payments to forty (40.0%) percent of the Professional Fee.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.3

q: The Architect's Guidelines on Methods of Compensation (UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210) explicitly replaces which earlier document?
o: 1979 UAP Doc. 208-b (Methods of Compensation and Schedule of Fees)
1960 Architects' National Code in its entirety
n: Section 1 states the new document replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 208-b (Methods of Compensation and Schedule of Fees).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 1

q: Continuing that scenario, how much ADDITIONAL payment is due upon completion of the Design Development Phase, given that cumulative payments must reach 40% of the P5,000,000 PF (having already reached 20% after Schematic Design)?
n: Cumulative target after DD = 40% x P5,000,000 = P2,000,000; already paid (20%) = P1,000,000; additional due = P2,000,000 - P1,000,000 = P1,000,000, matching the 20% increment stated in Sec. 6.4.3.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.3
scenario: Scenario: A Client and Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of P5,000,000 for Regular Design Services, to be paid per the Sec. 6.4 cumulative payment schedule (5% / 20% / 40% / 90% / 90% / 100% cumulative).

q: The Architect's Guidelines took effect how many days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation?
n: The Resolution states the Resolution and its Annex 'shall take effect after fifteen (15) days following their publication.'  Source: PRBoA Resolution No. 06, s. 2016

q: Under Sec. 6.4.6, the remaining 10% of the Professional Fee due at/after the Construction Phase is broken down into what two 5% components?
o: Architect's Liability under the Civil Code, and Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS)
n: Sec. 6.4.6 breaks the remaining 10% into: (a) 5% for the Architect's Liability under the Civil Code, and (b) 5% for Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.6

q: According to the Postscript, on what date was the New/Updated Standards of Professional Practice (SPP) approved and prescribed by the PRC through PRBoA Resolution No. 3?
n: The Postscript states the SPP was approved and subsequently prescribed by the PRC through PRBoA Resolution No. 3 on July 27, 2010, after 31 years.  Source: Postscript; PRBoA Resolution No. 03, s. 2010

q: Per Sec. 6.4.10, if the suspension of construction exceeds a period of how many months, the fee for the remaining Periodic Construction Supervision works shall be DOUBLED?
n: Sec. 6.4.10 states that when the suspension of construction exceeds a period of six (6) months, the fee for the remaining works (Periodic Construction Supervision) shall be doubled.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.10

q: The three pre-UAP architectural organizations that were unified on December 12, 1974 into the United Architects of the Philippines were the PIA, the LPA, and which other organization?
o: Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
Council of the Built and Natural Environment (CBNE)
n: The Postscript names the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA), the League of Philippine Architects (LPA), and the Association of Philippine Government Architects (APGA) as the three organizations integrated into the UAP.  Source: Postscript

q: Which fee adjustment factor addresses the need for a Building Information Model (BIM) and multiple electronic document formats for different parties?
n: Sec. 6.5.1 (Project Documentation) discusses unique documentation forms, BIM requirements, and multiple electronic formats as a factor requiring fee adjustment.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.5.1

q: Per Sec. 3 (Criteria), the Architect's compensation should be based on mutual evaluation of which of the following?
o: The amount of the Architect's/firm's talents, skill, experience, effort and time required by the project
Only the Architect's years in practice
n: Section 3 states the criteria for computing compensation is based on mutual evaluation of the Architect's/firm's talents, skill, experience, effort, and time available for and required by the project.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 3 (Criteria)

q: When using the Percentage of Cost of Work method for Specialized Architectural Services (Sec. 7.2.2), what does the Architect's Fee EXCLUDE?
o: The fee of any Engineering and/or Specialist Consultants (SCs) working with the Architect
n: Sec. 7.2.2 states that when using the Percentage of Cost of Work, the Architect's Fee excludes the fee of any Engineering and/or Specialist Consultants working with the Architect.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.2.2

q: The 2010 SPP Documents classify methods of Architect's compensation into which three main types?
o: Design fee, Supervision fee, and Consulting fee
Government rate, Private rate, and Foreign rate
Percentage-based Fee, Lump Sum or Fixed Fee, and Time basis
n: Sec. 4 states compensation methods are generally classified into three main types: a) Percentage-based Fee, b) Lump Sum or Fixed Fee, and c) Time basis.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4

q: A Client separately engages a lighting Specialist Consultant (SC) whose fee is P2,000,000, while the project Architect coordinates the SC's work with the overall design. What is the Architect's coordination fee under Sec. 7.2.3?
n: Coordination fee = 5% x P2,000,000 = P100,000, per Sec. 7.2.3.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.2.3
scenario: Scenario: A Client separately engages a lighting design Specialist Consultant (SC) whose fee is P2,000,000, while the project Architect coordinates and relates the SC's work to the overall design concept.

q: Charges based on a percentage of construction cost may be pegged to which THREE bases under Sec. 4.1.1.3?
n: Sec. 4.1.1.3.1-3 lists the Probable Project Construction Cost (PPCC), the Awarded Project Construction Cost (APCC, based on the winning bid), and the Final Project Construction Cost (FPCC, based on Cost Records).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.3

q: Under Sec. 7.3.2.1, what is the Recommended Professional Fee for Physical Planning of building sites, per hectare, for the first five (5) hectares?
n: Sec. 7.3.2.1 states the RPF is P50,000.00 per hectare for the first five (5) hectares net to the Architect.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.2.1

q: What is the difference between DAEDS and DADS as defined in Sec. 4.1.1.4-4.1.1.5?
o: DAEDS is time-based; DADS is always a lump sum
There is no difference; the terms are synonymous
DAEDS is a single contract covering architectural + basic engineering design; DADS excludes engineering fees and uses separate contracts
DAEDS is only for residential projects; DADS is only for commercial projects
n: DAEDS (Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services) is a single, complete architectural-and-engineering contract; DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services) excludes engineering/specialist consultant fees, with the Architect as lead/prime professional.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.4-4.1.1.5

q: A physical planning engagement covers 8 hectares of land ('Over 5 hectares up to 10 hectares' bracket: P250,000.00 + P40,000.00 per hectare in excess of 5 hectares). What is the Recommended Professional Fee?
n: Excess over 5 ha = 3 ha; 3 x P40,000 = P120,000; RPF = P250,000 + P120,000 = P370,000.00.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.2 (Physical Planning fee table)
scenario: Scenario: A physical planning engagement (Site Development Planning, Sec. 7.3.2) covers a total land area of 8 hectares, moderately flat terrain.

q: A project's Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) professional fee is computed at P10,000,000. If the Owner instead contracts the Architect under DADS (engaging engineers separately), what is the Architect's DADS-equivalent architectural fee share?
n: Per Sec. 4.1.1.5, the architectural design services constitute 60% of the stated DAEDS professional fee: 60% x P10,000,000 = P6,000,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.5
scenario: Scenario: A commercial office project has a computed Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) professional fee of P10,000,000.

q: Under Sec. 7.3.2.3, the physical planning payment schedule allocates 30% of RPF to which of the two earliest planning outputs?
o: Framework Development Plan (FRDP) and Conceptual Master Development Plan (CMDP)
Only the Detailed Master Development Plan (DMDP)
Preliminary Master Development Plan (PMDP) and Detailed Master Development Plan (DMDP)
n: Sec. 7.3.2.3 allocates 30% of RPF each to the Framework Development Plan (FRDP) and the Conceptual Master Development Plan (CMDP), and 20% each to the Preliminary (PMDP) and Detailed (DMDP) Master Development Plans.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.2.3

q: Continuing the same Unit Cost Method example, what is the TOTAL Professional Fee for DAEDS Services (GFA portion plus non-GFA portion, the latter billed at 50% of the GFA rate)?
n: PF for GFA = P1,800/sqm x 10,000 sqm = P18,000,000; PF for non-GFA (at 50% of GFA rate, i.e. P900/sqm) x 2,000 sqm = P1,800,000; total = P19,800,000.00, matching the worked example.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.2 (Unit Cost Method example)
scenario: Scenario (Unit Cost Method worked example): A high-rise office building project has 10,000 sqm gross floor area (GFA) and 2,000 sqm non-GFA. Average Project Construction Cost (based on historical data) is P30,000.00/sqm, and the Professional Fee based on Percentage of PCC is 6%.

q: Under Sec. 8.3, the Recommended Professional Fee for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services is what percentage of the Project Construction Cost?
n: Sec. 8.3 states the RPF for Fulltime Construction Supervision Services is 1% to 1.5% of the PCC.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 8.3

q: Continuing that scenario, what is the combined Professional Fee for BOTH the GFA and non-GFA portions (non-GFA billed at 50% of the GFA per-sqm rate)?
n: Non-GFA PF = P625/sqm (50% of P1,250) x 1,500 sqm = P937,500; total = P10,000,000 + P937,500 = P10,937,500.00.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.2 (Unit Cost Method)
scenario: Scenario: An office building project has 8,000 sqm gross floor area (GFA) and 1,500 sqm non-GFA. Average Project Construction Cost is P25,000.00/sqm, and the applicable percentage for professional fee based on PCC is 5%.

q: For the same P40,000,000 project, what is the HIGHEST reasonable Full-Time Supervision fee under the 1%-1.5% range?
n: Highest RPF = 1.5% x P40,000,000 = P600,000, per Sec. 8.3.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 8.3
scenario: Scenario: A project with a Project Construction Cost of P40,000,000 engages a Consulting Architect for Full-Time Construction Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A).

q: Under the Lump Sum or Fixed Fee method (Sec. 4.2), which TWO approaches are generally used to arrive at the lump-sum compensation?
o: Man-hours multiplied by a factor of 3.0 only
A monthly retainer and an hourly rate
The Awarded and Final PCC only
A percentage of probable construction cost, and direct estimation of cost elements plus profit margin
n: Sec. 4.2.2.1-4.2.2.2 describes computing a lump sum as an appropriate percentage of the probable construction cost, or directly developing a fixed amount by estimating individual cost elements plus a reasonable profit margin — often used together as a check on each other.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.2.2

q: Under Sec. 9.3, the Recommended Professional Fee for the Architect acting as Construction Manager (CM) is what percentage of the PCC?
n: Sec. 9.3 states the RPF for Construction Management Services is 1.5% to 3% of the Project Construction Cost (PCC).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 9.3

q: The two types of fee multipliers described under hourly billing (Sec. 4.3.5) are a multiplier of Direct Salary Expenses and a multiplier of:
n: Sec. 4.3.5 identifies two multiplier types: one of 'Direct Salary Expenses' and another (the most common) of 'Direct Personnel Expenses.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.5

q: Which incentive-type contract, under Sec. 9.2.2.3, pays the Construction Manager a fee that is unaffected by variations between estimate and bids, unless the Owner increases scope?
n: Sec. 9.2.2.3 (Firm Fixed Price) states the Owner pays a fixed fee unaffected by variations between the estimate and bids or by change orders, unless the Owner initiates a scope increase.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 9.2.2.3

q: Under the formula 'Fee = Direct Cost x M,' if the Direct Cost (sum of Architect's, Consultants', and Technical Staff's hourly charges for hours spent) is P400,000 and the office applies a multiplier of 2.0, what is the Fee (before adding reimbursable expenses)?
n: Fee = Direct Cost x M = P400,000 x 2.0 = P800,000, per the Sec. 4.3.8 formula (Direct cost = An + Cn + Tn; Fee = Direct Cost x M).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.8 (Formula)
scenario: Scenario: An architectural office computes a Direct Cost (Architect + Consultant + Technical staff hourly charges, i.e. An + Cn + Tn) of P400,000 for a project, using a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit.

q: Under Sec. 10.3, the Recommended Professional Fee based on value-pricing for Post-Construction/Building Administration Services is:
n: Sec. 10.3 states the RPF based on value-pricing is from 4% to 6% of gross rental.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 10.3

q: Under the Salary method (Sec. 4.3.11), the formula 'Fee = Salary Cost x Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses' typically uses a multiplier starting from what value?
n: Sec. 4.3.11.1 states this method multiplies the total basic salaries (Direct Salary Expenses) of the PCAs and staff 'by a factor from 3.0 as a multiplier' plus reimbursable expenses.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.11.1

q: Under Sec. 11.3.1, the Architect acting as Project Manager for Comprehensive Architectural Services is entitled to what RPF, as a percentage of PCC?
n: Sec. 11.3.1 states the RPF for Project Manager is 2% to 5% of Project Construction Cost (PCC).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 11.3.1

q: The Retainer method of compensation (Sec. 4.3.13) is best described as:
o: A one-time lump sum paid only at project completion
A method that can never include per diem or hourly add-ons
A stipulated amount paid at regular intervals ensuring the PCA's availability, with additional services billed separately
A method exclusively used for expert witness testimony
n: Sec. 4.3.13.1 describes the retainer as a stipulated amount paid at regular intervals to ensure availability of the PCA's services, covering minimum required services, with all additional services paid separately.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.13.1

q: Per Sec. 11.3.2, if the Architect-Project Manager ALSO performs Regular Design Services on the same project, how is that portion compensated?
o: It is included in the Project Manager fee with no extra charge
It is compensated separately, as stipulated in SPP Doc. 202
It is billed only as a per diem
n: Sec. 11.3.2 states that if the Project Manager also performs Regular Design Services, he is compensated separately for those services as stipulated in SPP Doc. 202.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 11.3.2

q: How many major categories of Architectural Services does Rule III (Schedule of Fees) divide the entire range of Architect's services into?
n: Rule III states the entire range of the Architect's services is divided into ten (10) major services, from Pre-Design Services (SPP Doc. 201) through Professional Architectural Consulting Services (SPP Doc. 209).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Rule III

q: Under Sec. 12.4.2, the Recommended Professional Fee for Design-Build Services on a GUARANTEED MAXIMUM COST basis is what percentage of PCC?
n: Sec. 12.4.2 states the RPF for Design-Build Services on a Guaranteed Maximum Cost basis is 10% of the PCC (or already built into the GMC), exclusive of the Regular Design Services fee.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 12.4.2

q: Under Sec. 5 (Pre-Design Services, SPP Doc. 201), what acceptance fee percentage of the agreed Professional Fee should the Architect request upon signing the Professional Service Agreement?
n: Sec. 5.3 states the Architect should request a five percent (5%) acceptance fee based on the agreed professional fee (PF) upon signing of the agreement.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 5.3
